title: Risotto con Frutti di Mare
subtitle: Mixed seafood risotto with clams, mussels, and prawns
excerpt: Risotto con frutti di mare is a celebration seafood risotto: clams, mussels, and prawns cooked in white wine and combined with a rich seafood-stock risotto. Each type of shellfish cooks briefly in white wine and contributes its liquor to the stock. The finished risotto is glossy, briny, and fragrant with parsley.
sourceNotes: Mixed seafood risotto is found across the Italian Adriatic and Tyrrhenian coastlines. It is one of the most festive versions of the dish, served at Christmas Eve dinners (the feast of seven fishes) and at summer seafood restaurants along the coast.

content.text: The key to mixed seafood risotto is cooking each type of shellfish separately in white wine, collecting all the liquor, and using it as part of the stock. The seafood goes back in only at the very end. This way nothing is overcooked and the stock is full of flavour from all three types of shellfish.

Open {{clams}} clams and {{mussels}} mussels separately in batches in a covered pan with a splash of {{white-wine-dry}} wine over high heat. Each takes 3 to 4 minutes. Discard any that do not open. Strain all liquor through a fine sieve and combine. Remove most shellfish from their shells, leaving some in shell for presentation.

Combine the shellfish liquor with enough water to make 1.2 litres of liquid. Keep hot. Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil in a heavy pan over medium heat. Cook {{onion}} onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{chilli-flakes}} chilli (if using).

Add {{carnaroli-rice}} rice and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the remaining {{white-wine-dry}} wine and stir until absorbed. Add the hot shellfish stock a ladleful at a time for 18 minutes until the rice is al dente.

Stir in the clam and mussel meat, then the {{prawns-raw}} prawns. Cook for 90 seconds until the prawns turn pink. Stir in {{parsley-flat}} parsley. Taste for {{salt-table}} salt. Serve at once with the reserved shellfish in shell on top.

items.symptom: The seafood is overcooked and rubbery
items.cause: Added too early or left in the pan too long.
items.fix: All the shellfish must go in at the very end. The prawns need only 90 seconds. Shellfish toughens quickly and cannot be revived. Have everything ready before the rice finishes cooking.

content.text: Mixed seafood risotto is the centrepiece of the Italian Christmas Eve dinner in coastal areas, part of the Feast of the Seven Fishes tradition. It is also the showpiece of Italian summer seafood restaurants. In Venice it is called risotto ai frutti di mare and is made with whatever the Rialto market offers. No cheese -- ever.
